en.title: Nightcrawler's Secret Family Ties Just Got Weirder on X-Men '97
en.summary: The latest episode of X-Men '97 threw fans for a loop with unexpected family revelations for Kurt Wagner. Prepare for a deep dive into a lineage that's far more tangled than it appears.
en.body:
The **X-Men '97** team has always been a family, but the latest installment, "Strange Land, Savage Heart," throws a particularly baffling wrench into the definition of kinship for our favorite fuzzy blue mutant, **Nightcrawler**. In a plot that feels like a courtroom drama transplanted to a prehistoric jungle, **Kurt Wagner** finds himself defending the indefensible – **Graydon Creed**, an anti-mutant bigot – against the zealous **Exodus** and his Acolytes. Amidst the chaos of the Savage Land, the proceedings take a bewildering turn when **Nightcrawler** refers to **Rogue** as his sister and **Graydon Creed** as his brother.

This isn't the first time **Nightcrawler's** origins have been hinted at as complex. When **Kurt Wagner** first arrived in the comics in 1975, he was a lone figure fleeing persecution. His upbringing with the sorceress **Margali Szardos** and his connection to **Amanda Sefton** were revealed later. However, the seeds of a much stranger familial web were sown by none other than **Mystique** herself in 1981, hinting at a shared connection with **Kurt**. This ambiguity has long been a hallmark of **Chris Claremont's** legendary run, often playing with character relationships and identities in ways that pushed the boundaries of superhero storytelling.

## A Mystique-al Lineage

For long-time comic readers, **Mystique's** connection to **Nightcrawler** isn't exactly new, but its explicit acknowledgment and the way it's presented within the animated series adds a fresh layer of intrigue. **Mystique**, a shapeshifter with a penchant for manipulation and a history intertwined with many mutant lineages, is indeed **Kurt Wagner's** mother. This revelation, often explored in the comics, adds a profound, albeit dark, dimension to **Kurt's** constant search for belonging and his struggle with his demonic appearance. The fact that he could be related to figures like **Rogue** (through shared connections or adoption within the X-Men's found family) and even his ideological opposite **Graydon Creed** (whose own parentage is famously tied to **Mystique** and **Sabretooth**) creates a narrative knot that the show is expertly beginning to untangle.

## The Fan Reaction to a Twisted Family Tree

For fans of **X-Men '97**, these revelations are more than just plot twists; they are the culmination of decades of comic lore brought to vibrant animated life. The show has consistently leaned into the rich history of the **X-Men** comics, delighting long-time followers while remaining accessible to newcomers. The complex parentage of **Nightcrawler**, particularly his ties to **Mystique**, is a pivotal piece of his character. Seeing it play out on screen, especially in such an unexpected context as a trial in the Savage Land, sparks passionate discussion online about how these established comic storylines will be adapted and what further surprises await.

## What's Next for the Wagner Family

As **X-Men '97** continues its second season, expect these intricate family dynamics to be a central focus. The showrunners have a deep understanding of the source material, and the implications of **Nightcrawler's** complicated lineage, especially his relationship with **Mystique**, are likely to have significant narrative consequences for the rest of the season and beyond. The exploration of these tangled threads promises to deliver more emotional depth and shocking twists.

content_raw: This article contains spoilers for X-Men ’97 season 2 episode 7 . On its surface, the latest episode of X-Men ’97 , “Strange Land, Savage Heart,” plays like a standard legal drama, just with mutants. The Catholic Nightcrawler, always the moral compass of the team, volunteers to argue in defense of the anti-mutant bigot Graydon Creed against the fundamentalist Exodus, leader of the Acolytes. Along the way, the story has plenty of space for over-the-top action, not just because the trial takes place in the Savage Land, a place in Marvel ‘s Antartica that remains in its prehistoric state. But things start to get confusing right at the beginning, when the demonic-looking, blue-fur-covered Nightcrawler refers to Southern Belle Rogue as his sister. Even more confusing, he calls the blond-haired human Creed his brother. But if you think that’s weird, just wait until you read about how Nightcrawler is kin to these and other X-characters. Mystique’s Family Tree When Kurt Wagner a.k.a. Nightcrawler first appeared in 1975’s Giant-Size X-Men #1, he’s alone and being chased by his German countrymen. We don’t really uncover much more about his backstory until Uncanny X-Men Annual #4 (1980), in which we learn about how he was raised by the witch Margali Szardos, alongside his “sister”/girlfriend Amanda Sefton. But almost immediately afterward, in 1981’s Uncanny X-Men #142 by Chris Claremont and John Byrne, the blue-skinned shapeshifter Mystique hinted that she and Kurt may share a familial connection. A lot of things get hinted at during Claremont’s legendary 17-year run on Uncanny X-Men , mostly involving sexual orientation. Many of the characters were written to be queer, but Marvel editorial and the Comics Code Authority (the industry-regulated censorship board) refused any open same-sex relationships. Thus, Mystique and the seer Destiny were always explicitly described as just really good friends. However, on a less despairing note, Claremont also liked to use shadowy backstories as part of his plotting, setting up things like the truth of Wolverine’s origin or the mystery of the third Summers brother as a engine that would drive future stories. By the mid-’90s, however, Claremont had left the franchise and others took over, people who wanted to pay off plot lines set up earlier. Thus, in 1994’s X-Men Unlimited #4, by Scott Lobdell and Richard Bennett, we finally definitively learn that Mystique is Nightcrawler’s parent. That issue also makes clear that, by extension, Nightcrawler is the brother to Rogue, in deed if not biology. In her first appearance in 1981’s Avengers Annual #10 , by Claremont and Michael Golden, Rogue was a youthful member of the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants, then led by Mystique.
